**Produced.** `docs/spikes/2026-09-12-ledger-database.md` (about 10,900 words) with the ten sections in the mandated order; question 8 is answered as an H3 inside the Migration plan so the ten-section order holds. Each of the eight Appendix A questions has one recommendation and the evidence behind it: SQLite in WAL mode, one database at `.spud/ledger.db` in Spud's home (gitignored, `SPUD_HOME` resolution, worktree-safe); a schema of `projects`, `tickets`, `members` (lineage as a materialized path; `SPUD-002/01.01` is one row; every limit is a `count(*)` inside the insert transaction), `spawn_requests`, append-only `events`, `handoffs`, `proposals` + `proposal_decisions`, `name_pool`, `renders`, with views and an ownership matrix; WAL + `busy_timeout` + `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` from every process, no daemon and no MCP writer; import-once, render-always migration with the markdown committed and the database ignored; Python 3.14 stdlib as `bin/spud` invoked `python3.14 -I -S`; an enforcement plan that moves Laws 3, 4, 6, 7, the path rule and the finishing rule into hooks and the CLI, with the `agent_id` mapping solved through `tool_use_id`; a generated Team card plus `Fleet.base#Team` with `ticket == this` for Eric's per-ticket view, and reports rendered from events. Nine ticket proposals and nine open questions for Eric.

**Team.** [[SPUD-006/Elba|Elba]] (01.01, contractor on claude-code-guide, sonnet) verified the Claude Code facts against raw page source and cited them; [[SPUD-006/Dakota|Dakota]] (01.02, scout, haiku) cited the Obsidian Bases facts. Both accepted, both `done`, Outcomes written, no proposals from either.

**Verified on this machine (2026-09-12).** Runtime inventory and SQLite versions per runtime; cold-start latency of 15 cases, 21 timed runs each (Python 3.14 hook-shaped 18.3 ms median, `-S` 17.2; Node 26.0; Bun 12.9; sqlite3 CLI 3.4); WAL contention with 9 and 30 concurrent writer processes and a Python+Node+Bun mix (0 errors with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` + 5 s timeout; 995 and 1056 errors in the two trap configurations); JSON1, FTS5, RETURNING, STRICT available in all three runtimes; four headless `claude -p` probes capturing real `PreToolUse`, `SubagentStart`, `PostToolUse` and `SubagentStop` payloads, the foreground and background `Agent` return shapes, the presence of `agent_id` inside subagents, the `meta.json` timing, and a live Python SQLite hook writing all six events; the Agent tool's return metadata quoted verbatim from my own two children (`subagent_tokens`, `tool_uses`, `duration_ms`). Documentation quotes for SQLite, DuckDB, `node:sqlite`, Obsidian Bases and Claude Code hooks/sub-agents/permissions/settings are cited by URL.

**Left.** Nothing blocks the recommendation. Nine questions for Eric are in the spike (database location, ticket numbering across projects, fan-out semantics, hand edits in Obsidian, the two spawn-convention changes, enforcement strictness at launch, generated reports, other repositories, durability pragma); I recommended an answer to each. Not measured: Obsidian's pickup of externally written files while the vault is open (undocumented; the first `spud render` is the check), and the ordering of `SubagentStart` events when several foreground spawns are issued in one message (avoided by the background-spawn default). Scratch scripts and probe sessions stayed under the session scratchpad; nothing was written to the repo outside the spike and the three SPUD-006 team files.

members.result:
<!-- the spudagent: the seven answers, format per the brief, plus Sources -->

**Method note.** For the huge `hooks` reference page, WebFetch's small summarizing model gave inconsistent, sometimes fabricated answers on specific field names across repeated identical-intent queries (worst case: four different guesses — `tool_output`, "not present", `tool_output` again with a non-matching quoted context, `tool_result` — for one field that is actually `tool_response`). I downloaded the raw `.md` source with `curl` and verified every fact below against that raw text with `grep`/`awk`. Quotes below are ground-truth verbatim from the raw source unless marked otherwise.

---

### Q1 — Hook events; SubagentStart/SubagentStop

**Full event list (33).** `SessionStart`, `Setup`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch`, `Notification`, `MessageDisplay`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `TaskCreated`, `TaskCompleted`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `TeammateIdle`, `InstructionsLoaded`, `ConfigChange`, `CwdChanged`, `DirectoryAdded`, `FileChanged`, `WorktreeCreate`, `WorktreeRemove`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `PreModelSwitch`, `PostModelSwitch`, `Elicitation`, `ElicitationResult`, `SessionEnd`.
Quote: "Claude Code fires hook events at specific points in its lifecycle." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide

**SubagentStart input.** Common fields (`session_id`, `prompt_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `scratchpad_dir`, `permission_mode`, `hook_event_name`, `effort`) plus `agent_id`, `agent_type`.
Quote: "SubagentStart hooks receive `agent_id` with the unique identifier for the subagent and `agent_type` with the agent name" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart

**SubagentStop input.** Common fields plus `stop_hook_active`, `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `agent_transcript_path`, `last_assistant_message`, and (shared with `Stop`) `background_tasks`, `session_crons`.
Quote: "SubagentStop hooks receive `stop_hook_active`, `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `agent_transcript_path`, and `last_assistant_message`" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstop

**What each may return.** `SubagentStart` cannot block; it can only inject context. `SubagentStop` can block (delays teardown) via the `Stop`-style `decision`/`reason` format.
Quotes: "SubagentStart hooks can't block subagent creation, but they can inject context into the subagent." / "Returning `decision: \"block\"` with a `reason` keeps the subagent running and delivers `reason` to the subagent as its next instruction." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart and #subagentstop

**additionalContext: subagent or parent? (the key question).** `SubagentStart`'s `additionalContext` goes to the **subagent**, injected before its first turn, and persists as part of its instructions for the session. `SubagentStop`'s `additionalContext`/`decision:block` also stays with the **subagent** (it's delivered back to the subagent to keep it running) — it does **not** reach the parent. To put something in front of the parent/main session after a subagent finishes, the docs say to use a different hook entirely: `PostToolUse` matched on the `Agent` tool.
Quotes: "String added to the subagent's context at the start of its conversation, before its first prompt." (SubagentStart) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart
"To inject context into the parent session after a subagent returns, use a `PostToolUse` hook on the `Agent` tool instead." (SubagentStop) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstop
*(An earlier lower-fidelity fetch attempt had told me SubagentStop's context "is visible to the main conversation" — that was wrong; the raw source above corrects it.)*

---

### Q2 — PreToolUse / PostToolUse

**PreToolUse input.** `session_id`, `prompt_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `scratchpad_dir`, `permission_mode`, `hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`.
Quote: "The `tool_name`, `tool_input`, and `tool_use_id` fields are event-specific." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#pretooluse

**PostToolUse input.** `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_response`, `tool_use_id`, optional `duration_ms`. The result field is **`tool_response`**, not `tool_output` and not `tool_result` (both zero hits in the raw page; `tool_response` is the only one used, confirmed by direct grep after WebFetch gave three different wrong answers for this one field across attempts).
Quote: "The input includes both `tool_input`, the arguments sent to the tool, and `tool_response`, the result it returned." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#posttooluse

**Matcher syntax; does `"Agent"` match the Agent tool?** Tool events (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`) match on tool name; a matcher of only letters/digits/`_`/`-`/spaces/`,`/`|` is an exact string (or list) match, otherwise it's an unanchored JS regex. `Agent` is itself a documented canonical built-in tool name (the one that spawns subagents) in the tools reference, so a matcher of `"Agent"` matches it exactly the same way `"Bash"` matches Bash — the hooks page just doesn't happen to use `Agent` as one of its example matcher values.
Quotes: "`Bash` matches only the Bash tool; `Edit\|Write` and `Edit, Write` each match either tool exactly" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#matcher-patterns
"Spawns a [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) with its own context window to handle a task." (the `Agent` tool's own doc line) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference

**PreToolUse output.** Nested under `hookSpecificOutput`, not a top-level `decision`. Fields: `permissionDecision` (**four** values — `allow`/`deny`/`ask`/`defer`, one more than the brief's list), `permissionDecisionReason`, `updatedInput`, `additionalContext`.
Quote: "\"deny\" prevents the tool call. \"ask\" prompts the user to confirm. \"defer\" exits gracefully so the tool can be resumed later." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#pretooluse-decision-control

**Exit codes.** 0 = success (JSON on stdout is parsed and honored). 2 = the only code that blocks purely by virtue of the code itself, and it wins even over a JSON `permissionDecision: "allow"`. Anything else is non-blocking: the action proceeds; a validly-schema'd JSON payload is still honored, otherwise it's logged as a `<hook name> hook error`.
Quotes: "Exit 2 means a blocking error." / "Any other exit code doesn't block on its own for most hook events." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-2 and #other-exit-codes

---

### Q3 — Hooks inside subagents

Yes, confirmed directly and unambiguously: tool-use hooks fire for a subagent's own tool calls, using the same configured hooks as the main session, and the payload is tagged with `agent_id`/`agent_type` specifically so a hook can tell the two apart.
Quotes: "When a subagent calls a tool, tool events such as `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` fire the same configured hooks as in the main conversation" / "the input carries the `agent_id` and `agent_type` common input fields that identify the subagent" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks
Corroborating, on background subagents specifically: "Claude Code still runs the hooks for their tool calls, and if no hook returns a decision, it denies the call." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide

---

### Q4 — Agent tool result metadata (parent's view)

Documented, but **not on the sub-agents page** the brief pointed at — the telemetry table actually lives on the **hooks** page, under the `Agent` tool's entry for what a `PostToolUse` hook's `tool_response` carries. The sub-agents page documents only the agent ID and the resume mechanism.
- sub-agents page: agent ID received; resumable via `SendMessage`. Quotes: "When a subagent completes, Claude receives its agent ID." / "Claude uses the `SendMessage` tool with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field to resume it." — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents
- hooks page (`PostToolUse` on the `Agent` tool): `status`, `agentId`, `content` (final text blocks), `resolvedModel`, `modelsUsed`, **`totalTokens`**, **`totalDurationMs`**, **`totalToolUseCount`**, and `usage` (`input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens`/`cache_read_input_tokens`). So yes to all four things the brief asked about: duration, tokens, tool-use count, and agent id are all documented, just on the hooks page rather than the sub-agents page.
Quotes: "your PostToolUse hook receives the subagent's final text and run telemetry in `tool_response`" / "Wall-clock duration of the subagent run" (`totalDurationMs`) / "Count of tool calls the subagent made" (`totalToolUseCount`) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#agent

---

### Q5 — Sub-agent configuration

**`model` values.** `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full model ID, or `inherit`.
Quote: "Model to use: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full model ID such as `claude-opus-5`, or `inherit`" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields

**`isolation: worktree`.** Documented: runs the subagent's Bash/PowerShell commands inside a temporary git worktree branched from the default branch, auto-cleaned up if it makes no changes.
Quote: "Set to `worktree` to run the subagent in a temporary git worktree, giving it an isolated copy of the repository" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields

**"fork".** Not a `subagent_type` value — it's a mode of the `Agent` tool call ("fork the current conversation" / `/subtask`) that drops the normal isolation and inherits the whole conversation, including the model.
Quotes: "A fork is a subagent that inherits the entire conversation so far instead of starting fresh." / "a fork sees the same system prompt, tools, model, and message history as the main session" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#fork-the-current-conversation

**`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`.** Documented. Default nesting depth is 3 layers below the main conversation; the variable changes it.
Quotes: "a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation" / "set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to the number of subagent layers you want below your main conversation" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#let-subagents-spawn-their-own-subagents

**`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`.** Documented. Default cap is 20 concurrently-running subagents per session (ultracode-effort sessions are exempt).
Quote: "when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached`" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents

---

### Q6 — Hook configuration

**Where hooks may be defined.** Seven documented locations: `~/.claude/settings.json` (user), `.claude/settings.json` (project), `.claude/settings.local.json` (project local), managed policy settings, a plugin's `hooks/hooks.json`, skill frontmatter, and subagent frontmatter. The `--settings` CLI flag is not named as its own row in that table, but it can carry a `hooks` block too, since it accepts arbitrary settings JSON for the session.
Quotes: "Where you define a hook determines its scope" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#configure-hook-location
"It can set any key your user settings file can set; it can't set `Managed` or `Global config` keys." (of `--settings`) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#change-a-setting-for-one-session

**Workspace trust.** More nuanced than a flat yes/no. Hooks defined in settings files are **not** gated by trust of the exact folder — they run once a parent folder is trusted, and even in a `claude -p`/SDK run where the folder was never trusted at all. That's a real contrast with `permissions.allow`/`additionalDirectories`, which do wait on the exact folder's trust dialog. Separately, a project **subagent's own frontmatter hooks** specifically are withheld until that exact folder is trusted, silently, with no dialog offered for them.
Quotes: "Hooks in settings files, the env block and helper commands such as apiKeyHelper, and a project skill's hooks and allowed-tools" → both listed columns say "Used" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#what-runs-before-you-trust-a-folder
"Not used, and no dialog is offered" (frontmatter hooks in a project subagent, specifically) — same URL

**Default hook timeout.** Varies by hook type: `command`/`http`/`mcp_tool` = 10 minutes (lowered to 30s for `UserPromptSubmit`/`PreModelSwitch`/`PostModelSwitch`, 10s for `MessageDisplay`); `prompt` = 30 seconds; `agent` = 60 seconds; `SessionEnd` hooks of any type share a 1.5s budget (raised to match a longer configured `timeout`, up to 60s).
Quote: "Claude Code lowers this default to 30 seconds for `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreModelSwitch`, and `PostModelSwitch` hooks, and to 10 seconds for `MessageDisplay`" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#limitations

**Parallel execution.** Yes, confirmed directly.
Quote: "Claude Code runs all matching hooks in parallel" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide

**Hook types.** Five, not three: `command` (default), `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt`, `agent`.
Quote: "`type` ... `\"command\"`, `\"http\"`, `\"mcp_tool\"`, `\"prompt\"`, or `\"agent\"`" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#common-fields

---

### Q7 — Transcripts

**Does a subagent have its own transcript file?** Yes, a separate file per subagent, keyed by agent ID, persisting independently of the main conversation.
Quote: "find IDs in the transcript files at `~/.claude/projects/{project}/{sessionId}/subagents/`. Each transcript is stored as `agent-{agentId}.jsonl`" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents

**Does a hook payload name it?** Yes — but only on `SubagentStop`, via a field distinct from the common `transcript_path` (which always stays the *main* session's transcript, even inside a subagent hook call). `SubagentStop`'s own `agent_transcript_path` field is the one that names the subagent's own transcript.
Quote: "The `transcript_path` is the main session's transcript, while `agent_transcript_path` is the subagent's own transcript stored in a nested `subagents/` folder" — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstop

---

### Sources
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents

<!-- the spudagent: the seven answers, format per the brief, plus Sources -->

### 1. What a base can read

**Fact:** Bases read note properties (frontmatter), file metadata (name, folder, mtime, tags, links), and formulas. Cannot read external databases, JSON files, CSV files, or plugin APIs.

**Quote:** "All the data in Obsidian Bases is stored in your local Markdown files and their properties."

**URL:** https://obsidian.md/help/bases

---

### 2. Embedding syntax

**Fact:** Bases embed using wikilink syntax: `![[File.base]]` for the default view or `![[File.base#ViewName]]` for a specific view. Bases are defined in YAML code blocks but cannot be written inline as a fenced code block (code blocks define structure, not embed).

**Quote:** "embed base files in any other file using the `![[File.base]]` syntax" and "By default, the first view in your view list displays when embedded."

**URL:** https://obsidian.md/help/bases/views

---

### 3. Relative filters in embedded bases

**Fact:** When a base is embedded in a note, the `this` object refers to that embedding note's properties. Example: `file.hasLink(this.file)`, `this.file.folder`, `this.file.name`. Enables dynamic queries based on the containing document.

**Quote:** "When the base is embedded in another file, `this` points to properties of the embedding file"

**URL:** https://obsidian.md/help/bases/syntax

---

### 4. View types available

**Fact:** Available views are table, list, cards, Kanban, and map. Cards view is best for per-item cards with text summary, as it "Display files as a grid of cards" and "Lets you create gallery-like views."

**Quote:** "table, list, cards, Kanban, and map" and "Display files as a grid of cards"

**URL:** https://obsidian.md/help/bases/views

---

### 5. Grouping and aggregates

**Fact:** Views can group by one property only. Summaries support aggregates: numeric (Sum, Average, Min, Max, Range, Median, Std Dev), dates (Earliest, Latest, Range), boolean (Checked, Unchecked), general (Empty, Filled, Unique). Formula properties can render links via `link(path, display)` function.

**Quote:** "define custom summary formulas" and default summary types include "Average, Min, Max, Sum, Range, Median, Standard Deviation"

**URL:** https://obsidian.md/help/bases/syntax

---

### 6. .base file format and auto-reload

**Fact:** `.base` files are plain YAML conforming to Obsidian's base schema. Auto-reload behavior when `.base` or `.md` files are externally modified: **not documented**.

**Quote:** "Bases must be valid YAML conforming to the schema defined below."

**URL:** https://obsidian.md/help/bases/syntax

---

### 7. Minimum Obsidian version and plugin type

**Fact:** Minimum Obsidian version required for Bases: **not documented**. Bases is a **core plugin** (built-in), not a community plugin.

**Quote:** "Bases is a core plugin that lets you create database-like views of your notes."

**URL:** https://obsidian.md/help/bases

---

**Produced** (branch `worktree-spd-015-lead-hold`, uncommitted, in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/spd-015-lead-hold`): `bin/spud` — `hook_subagent_stop` now holds a live member once when *either* half of the finishing rule is open: its own Result/Blocked is missing, **or** a direct child of its own has returned unrecorded, **or** a direct child is still alive. New helpers beside it: `RESULT_HOLD` (today's Result sentence, lifted to a constant, byte for byte), `unrecorded_children()` (direct children with `stopped_at` set, empty `outcome`, status `active` — the shape `hook_stop` uses for Spud's children), `alive_children()` (direct children `planned` or `active` with no `stopped_at`), `finish_commands()`, `children_hold_reason()`, `alive_children_reason()`, `stop_hold_reason()`. `tests/test_hooks.py` — a new `LeadHoldTest` class (13 cases) beside `SubagentStopTest`. `tests/probes/headless.py` — rewritten summaries (capture-time stamps via a `capture.py` hook, nested agents labelled by their Agent description, the `task_started`/`task_progress`/`task_updated`/`task_notification`/`background_tasks_changed` system messages, full `subagent_stats`, a timeline of every subagent transcript, every member row) and three new scenarios: `lead-hold`, `lead-hold-fg`, `lead-running`. Nothing else touched; nothing committed.

**Verified.** Red first, twice: 8 of the first 9 cases failed before the change (the ninth — the guard that the Result-only reason is unchanged — passed), then 6 of 13 failed again when the still-alive cases were added. Whole suite against the final code: `Ran 220 tests in 121.565s` / `OK` (207 from SPD-008 plus 13), no `__pycache__`, every run with `SPUD_HOME` in a scratch directory. Three headless probes on haiku, one at a time, in scratch homes (about $0.22-0.25 each), plus an exploration run against the unmodified code:

1. **Exploration** (`lead-hold`, old code, 20:14-20:16): Kestrel spawned Russet in the background at spawn depth 2 and ended its turn "waiting" at 20:15:13 — the harness marked its task completed at that instant and its transcript has no entry afterwards. Russet was **not** killed (`subagent_stats.killed.parent` 0): it slept 20:15:15-20:15:45, recorded its Result at 20:15:46 and stopped at 20:15:48, 35 s after its lead was gone; **its completion notification went to the main session**. Spud's `Stop` named only Kestrel (Russet had no `stopped_at`, then its parent was still `active`), and the run ended with Russet `active`, Result recorded, no outcome: an orphan that left the session unrecorded.
2. **`lead-hold-fg`** (final code, 74 s): the foreground child returned recorded at 20:28:35; the lead's stop at 20:28:39 was held once — event `SPUD-001/Kestrel returned with 1 unrecorded child (SPUD-001/Russet); held once`, block `Law 9: 1 child you spawned returned and is not recorded: SPUD-001/Russet (01.01, scout), stopped 20:28. Record it with `spud --as a1a137e497ce336b3 member finish SPUD-001/Russet --status done|blocked|failed --outcome '<verdict>'`, and decide the proposals it filed, if any (…)`. The lead ran that exact command (Russet `done` 20:28:43), ran `spud proposal list --open` (none), stopped again at 20:28:50 and was let go silently; Spud's `Stop` then blocked the main session and main recorded the lead.
3. **`lead-hold`** (final code, 105 s): same with a background child — the lead waited inside its turn, Russet stopped 20:30:20, the lead was held once at 20:30:32, recorded Russet at 20:30:36, was let go at 20:30:43. No orphan, unlike the exploration run.
4. **`lead-running`** (final code, 107 s): the lead returned at once after spawning. Held once at 20:33:21 with the still-alive clause (`Law 9: 1 child you planned is still alive: SPUD-001/Russet (01.01, scout), running since 20:33. Ending your turn ends your run: a background child is not killed with you, its completion notification goes to the main session and its row is orphaned. Wait inside this turn (`spud member show SPUD-001/Russet` until the child's Result is there), then record it with …`), delivered as a `hook_blocking_error`; the lead then slept, polled `member show`, slept, and ran `member finish SPUD-001/Russet --status done` at 20:34:10; its second stop (20:34:14, `stop_hook_active` true) was let go with nothing unrecorded. The exploration run's orphan became a recorded child.

Live ledger untouched by tests and probes: 17 tickets, none past SPD-017, `spud card SPD-015` shows only me, 1 member alive (me); the main checkout's `.claude/settings.json` is byte-identical to the baseline (sha256 9a152156…fcdbf) and to the worktree's copy.

**Decisions the brief left open.**
- **Children still running (the open case): the hold covers them**, on this evidence: a subagent's turn end *is* its return (the harness completes its task at the stop), a background child is not killed with it, the child's completion notification goes to the main session, its row is orphaned, and in a `-p` run it left the session unrecorded altogether. A block is the only thing that keeps a lead alive long enough to collect its child, and `stop_hook_active` still lets the second stop through, so the cost of a lead that genuinely cannot wait is one turn. The reason tells it how to wait *inside* the turn (poll `spud member show <ref>`), and says plainly: if you cannot wait, say so and return, your parent records it.
- **A planned child never spawned is in the same list**, with its own sentence and the exact `spud --as <id> member finish <ref> --status failed --outcome '<why>'`: nobody else can ever spawn it (the spawn hook requires the caller to be the parent), Spud's `Stop` never names it (no `stopped_at`), and it holds a fan-out and a concurrency slot for ever. A reserved spawn that never bound is listed the same way.
- **Reason text.** One block, clauses in order: returned children, children still alive, then the Result sentence when that is missing too (` Then record your Result with …`) or ` Then return your summary.` when it is not. With no children of its own the reason is the old Result hold **byte for byte** (a test asserts it). Children are listed as `SPUD-nnn/<Name> (<lineage>, <persona>), stopped HH:MM` (returned) or `…, running since HH:MM` / `…, planned HH:MM and never spawned` (alive), HH:MM local from the stamp, ordered by `stopped_at` then id (returned) and by `spawned_at`/`planned_at` then id (alive). Every child gets its own exact command; the proposals clause (`spud proposal list --open`; `spud --as <id> proposal decide …`) rides with the returned clause only. The "wait inside this turn" sentence and its `member show` commands appear only when a child is actually running.
- **Events.** The held stop writes `member.stopped` with `held: true`, `unrecorded: <Result missing>`, and `unrecorded_children` / `alive_children` (refs) when non-empty; body `… returned without a Result and with 1 unrecorded child (SPUD-nnn/X); held once`. The let-go stop keeps `held: false, unrecorded, transcript_usage` and adds the same two lists when any remain, with the counts in the body. `stopped_at` is still stamped at the final stop only, and status is still never touched by the hook.
- **Scope kept.** `hook_stop` (Spud's Law 9 block) is unchanged; a test confirms Spud can record an orphaned grandchild once its lead is finished (`member finish` accepts an ancestor), and that the grandchild is not listed while the lead lives. The same blind spot in Spud's own `Stop` — planned-never-spawned and still-running orphans are invisible to it — is **proposal 14 (P3)**, not work I did.
- **Probe scaffolding**, worth knowing before reading the runs: the probe's `spudagent` system prompt now tells the agent to run the commands a hold names, and, when told to wait, to sleep with `python3.14 -I -S -c 'import time; time.sleep(20)'` and poll `member show` before finishing. Haiku followed it every time. In the `lead-running` run the *main* session then fumbled `member finish` ("team context error") and left Kestrel unrecorded at session end — the SPD-017 ergonomics problem again, not a hook fault.

**Prose Spud should change at merge** (my brief forbids me those files): (1) `.claude/agents/spudagent.md`, "## Finishing", the sentence "the `SubagentStop` hook holds you once if neither a Result nor a Blocked is recorded" — it now also holds you once when a child you spawned is unrecorded or still alive, and names the exact `member finish` command; (2) `.claude/agents/spudagent.md`, "## Sub-agents" step 3, and the "Limits" line of the brief template in `CLAUDE.md`: a background child is not killed when you return and its notification does not follow you, so wait for it *inside* your turn (poll `spud member show`) or spawn it in the foreground, and record a child you never spawned with `--status failed`; (3) `CLAUDE.md`, Ledger v1, the hooks bullet "A spudagent that returns without `member result` or `member block` is held once with the reason" — extend with "or with a child of its own unrecorded or still alive"; (4) `CLAUDE.md`, Law 9 — say that below Spud the same rule is now enforced by `SubagentStop` for every parent, not only by the `Stop` hook for Spud.

**Left.** Proposal 14 (Spud's `Stop` and children that never returned). A child that is resumed after a stop keeps its `stopped_at`, so it reads as "returned unrecorded" to its parent until it stops again — the same shape `hook_stop` has had since SPD-008, untouched here. Hook latency is unchanged (one extra indexed query per bound stop).
